title: Cabinet Temperature Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The freezer cabinet thermistor is open or shorted.
fullDescription: E1 on Galanz upright and chest freezers indicates the cabinet temperature sensor is providing readings outside the valid range. The compressor will run on a default duty cycle and will not respond to set-point changes.

causes.cause: Loose connector at the main board
Wiring damaged near the cabinet liner

symptoms: Set point adjustments have no effect

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug the freezer for 5 minutes and reconnect.

fixSteps.title: Inspect harness
fixSteps.instruction: Access the main board behind the rear lower panel. Reseat the sensor connector.

fixSteps.title: Test sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the thermistor and measure resistance. Approximately 16 kOhm at -10 C is typical. Out of range = replace.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install replacement thermistor in original clip and route harness clear of moving parts.

whenToCallPro: If the harness routes through a foamed-in liner.

faq.q: Can I keep using the freezer?
faq.a: Short term yes, but monitor temperature with an external thermometer.

title: Evaporator Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The evaporator coil thermistor is out of range.
fullDescription: On frost-free Galanz freezers an evaporator-mounted thermistor terminates defrost when the coil reaches a target temperature. E2 means this sensor is open or shorted, which on some models forces the unit to skip defrost.

causes.cause: Connector on the rear bulkhead unplugged

symptoms: Frost building up on the evaporator panel
Defrost cycle never seems to run

fixSteps.title: Manual defrost
fixSteps.instruction: Empty contents and unplug for 24 hours to fully clear ice from the evaporator.

fixSteps.title: Access the evaporator
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the rear interior panel screws. Locate the thermistor clipped to the suction line or coil.

fixSteps.title: Test and replace
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance at room temperature; replace if out of range. Reroute harness back through the existing path.

whenToCallPro: If frost continues to return after sensor replacement.

faq.a: Without the evaporator sensor the controller cannot accurately terminate defrost, so frost accumulates.

title: High Temperature Alarm
shortDescription: Cabinet temperature has stayed above the safety threshold for too long.
fullDescription: E3 indicates the freezer interior has been warmer than -9 C / 15 F for an extended period. It is informational and signals that food safety may be compromised. Common after long power outages or door left open.

causes.cause: Door left open or seal failure

fixSteps.title: Acknowledge the alert
fixSteps.instruction: Press the alarm/mute button and verify the door is fully closed.

fixSteps.title: Inspect contents
fixSteps.instruction: Discard items showing partial thaw beyond ice crystals. Refreeze still-frozen items.

fixSteps.title: Inspect gasket
fixSteps.instruction: Run a dollar bill around the gasket - it should drag. Replace gasket if leaking.

whenToCallPro: If the freezer is unable to recover normal temperatures within 24 hours.

faq.a: If items still have ice crystals they can be refrozen. Discard if fully thawed for over 4 hours.

title: Defrost System Failure
shortDescription: Defrost cycle did not complete - heater or thermal fuse fault.
fullDescription: E4 reports a defrost timeout. The controller energizes the defrost heater but does not see the bimetal open within the allowed time, indicating an open heater, open bimetal, or failed thermal fuse.
symptoms: Heavy frost on rear interior wall
Reduced cooling and longer compressor run

fixSteps.title: Manual defrost
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug, empty, and let the freezer thaw for 24 hours.

fixSteps.title: Test heater
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance across the heater terminals. Open = replace. Typical 20-40 Ohm.

fixSteps.title: Test bimetal
fixSteps.instruction: Place bimetal in a freezer for 15 minutes and measure for continuity. Should close cold.

fixSteps.title: Replace failed parts
fixSteps.instruction: Install new heater and/or bimetal as needed; reattach the rear panel.

whenToCallPro: If both heater and bimetal pass tests but E4 returns - main board is suspect.

faq.q: Can I run the freezer until I fix this?
faq.a: Yes for a short time, but expect ice buildup and reduced efficiency.

title: Evaporator Fan Failure
shortDescription: The internal circulation fan is not running at correct speed (frost-free models).
fullDescription: E5 indicates the evaporator fan, which circulates cold air over the freezer cabinet, is stalled or missing tach feedback. Without it, areas of the freezer warm up while the evaporator over-frosts.

causes.cause: Loose harness on the fan motor

symptoms: Soft food in front, hard at the back
Loud chirp that stops when door opens

fixSteps.title: Manual defrost
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 24 hours to clear any ice obstructing the fan.

fixSteps.title: Spin test
fixSteps.instruction: Remove rear evaporator panel and spin the fan blade by hand - it should move freely.

fixSteps.title: Replace fan motor
fixSteps.instruction: Install matching Galanz fan motor with correct blade orientation. Reseat harness.

whenToCallPro: If ice keeps refreezing on the fan after replacement, the defrost system is the root cause.

faq.q: Is E5 only on frost-free models?
faq.a: Yes - manual-defrost chest freezers have no internal fan.

title: Communication Error
shortDescription: Display board lost communication with the main control.
fullDescription: E6 reports loss of serial communication between the user interface and the main control board on Galanz frost-free freezers. The compressor may continue to run on its last set point but no settings can be changed.

causes.cause: Loose ribbon cable in the door hinge

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 5 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Reseat cable
fixSteps.instruction: Open the top hinge cap to access the cable between display and main board. Reseat firmly.

fixSteps.title: Replace boards
fixSteps.instruction: Replace UI display board first; if E6 persists, replace main control board.

whenToCallPro: If the main control board needs replacement.

faq.q: Will my food spoil during E6?
faq.a: Usually not - the main board keeps cooling at the last commanded set point.

title: Low Temperature Alarm
shortDescription: Cabinet has fallen below the minimum design temperature.
fullDescription: LO appears when the cabinet temperature is colder than approximately -28 C / -18 F for an extended time. Indicates a stuck closed compressor relay, a sensor reading low, or a control board fault keeping the compressor on.

causes.cause: Set-point in deepest setting and ambient very cold

symptoms: Heavy frost on items in the freezer

fixSteps.title: Verify set-point
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm the freezer is not set at maximum. Set to mid-range and wait 24 hours.

fixSteps.title: Test thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Measure cabinet thermistor resistance at known temperature. If reading shorted (very low resistance) replace.

fixSteps.title: Replace control board
fixSteps.instruction: If the relay is welded, replace the main control board.

whenToCallPro: If the compressor relay is welded - replacing the control board may not be cost-effective.

faq.a: Yes - excessive cold causes freezer burn and wastes energy.

title: Sensor Reads Above Range
shortDescription: Sensor reading is higher than the controller can interpret.
fullDescription: HI is a warning shown when a thermistor reads at the high extreme of its range, often indicating a shorted sensor wire to ground or a failed sensor.

causes.cause: Water intrusion in the sensor connector

symptoms: Compressor running continuously despite cold cabinet

fixSteps.title: Inspect connectors
fixSteps.instruction: Locate the thermistor connector and inspect for moisture or corrosion. Dry and reseat.

fixSteps.title: Test sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance at room temperature - should be ~5 kOhm at 25 C. Replace if shorted.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install a new thermistor in the same clip and route harness clear of moving parts.

whenToCallPro: If the wiring is damaged inside a foamed-in liner.

faq.q: Why does HI show with cold cabinet?
faq.a: The sensor incorrectly reports a hot reading, so the controller keeps cooling.

title: Power Failure Indicator
shortDescription: Freezer detected a recent loss of power.
fullDescription: PF indicates the freezer was powered off unexpectedly. Useful for confirming food safety after returning from time away.

fixSteps.title: Acknowledge alarm
fixSteps.instruction: Press the alarm/mute button to dismiss PF.

fixSteps.title: Verify food safety
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect contents - items still containing ice crystals can be refrozen.

fixSteps.title: Test outlet
fixSteps.instruction: If PF appears repeatedly without obvious outage, test the outlet voltage and inspect the breaker.

whenToCallPro: If PF appears with no outage and the outlet tests good - the main board's brownout detection may be defective.

faq.q: How long can a Galanz freezer keep food cold during a power outage?
faq.a: Approximately 24-48 hours if kept closed and full.

title: Door Ajar Alarm
shortDescription: The freezer door has been left open for too long.
fullDescription: dO is the door-ajar warning. Galanz freezers trigger after about 2 minutes with the door switch reading open. The unit beeps continuously and the interior light remains on.

fixSteps.title: Close the door firmly
fixSteps.instruction: Push the door closed and verify the entire perimeter seals.

fixSteps.title: Clear obstructions
fixSteps.instruction: Make sure baskets and items are properly seated.

fixSteps.title: Inspect gasket and switch
fixSteps.instruction: Replace torn gasket. Use a multimeter to test the door switch and replace if stuck.

faq.a: Press the alarm/mute button to silence the audible beep; the message clears once the door is closed.
